too like the lightning.title: Too Like the Lightning
too like the lightning.author: Ada Palmer
too like the lightning.why: A future of utopian cities and philosophical argument narrated in an 18th-century voice; hard going but rewarding for ambitious readers.

invisible cities.title: Invisible Cities
invisible cities.author: Italo Calvino
invisible cities.why: Marco Polo describes imaginary cities to Kublai Khan in short poetic chapters; readers call it mind-blowing.

rising.title: The Dark Is Rising
rising.author: Susan Cooper
rising.why: A boy discovers he is one of the Old Ones who fight the Dark in a wintry English setting; readers return to it.

migrations.title: Migrations
migrations.author: Charlotte McConaghy
migrations.why: A woman follows the last Arctic terns across the sea amid extinction; hopeful and sad.

quantum thief.title: The Quantum Thief
quantum thief.author: Hannu Rajaniemi
quantum thief.why: A trickster thief in a far-future Mars city; dense, clever and said to be the best of its kind.

rant.title: Rant
rant.author: Chuck Palahniuk
rant.why: An oral biography of a strange man who spreads a disease; rougher than other Palahniuk but rewarding.

being mortal.title: Being Mortal
being mortal.author: Atul Gawande
being mortal.why: A surgeon looks at ageing and dying and how to give people a better ending; recommended for everyone.

xx.title: XX
xx.author: Rian Hughes
xx.why: A designer's novel about a signal from space, built as a physical artefact with many documents; fans say it is perfect.

black company.title: The Black Company
black company.author: Glen Cook
black company.why: A grim mercenary company's chronicle in a ruthless war; the military fantasy readers recommend if you are bored of Sanderson.

dragons egg.title: Dragon's egg
dragons egg.author: Robert L. Forward
dragons egg.why: Tiny life forms on a neutron star evolve rapidly, a hard SF classic; readers like the alien idea.

half of a yellow sun.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
half of a yellow sun.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
half of a yellow sun.why: Three lives caught up in the Biafran war in Nigeria; moving and well praised.

milkman.title: Milkman
milkman.author: Anna Burns
milkman.why: A teen in a divided Northern Irish town is stalked by a paramilitary; stream-of-consciousness, tough but excellent.

light in august.title: Light in August
light in august.author: William Faulkner
light in august.why: People in the Mississippi town and a man's outsiderness; one of Faulkner's heavy novels with beauty.

empire of pain.title: Empire of Pain
empire of pain.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
empire of pain.why: How the Sackler family fuelled the opioid crisis, reported like a drama; depressing but gripping.

sellout.title: The Sellout
sellout.author: Paul Beatty
sellout.why: A man tries to bring back segregation in his town in a ferociously funny satire.

nation.title: Nation
nation.author: Terry Pratchett
nation.why: Two teens survive on an island after a tsunami and rethink faith; funny, brutal and moving.

where the crawdads sing.title: Where the Crawdads Sing
where the crawdads sing.author: Delia Owens
where the crawdads sing.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

butchers crossing.title: Butcher's Crossing
butchers crossing.author: John Williams
butchers crossing.why: A hunt for buffalo in 1870s Kansas that grinds the men down; a brutal literary western.

blood music.title: Blood Music
blood music.author: Greg Bear
blood music.why: A scientist's microscopic intelligences take over; weird and ahead of its time, more hard SF than horror.

rivers of london.title: Rivers of London
rivers of london.author: Ben Aaronovitch
rivers of london.why: A London policeman discovers magic and a dark ghostly murder; funny paranormal mystery.

beach music.title: Beach Music
beach music.author: Pat Conroy
beach music.why: A family secret and grief in South Carolina and France; emotionally devastating Southern saga.

da vinci code.title: The Da Vinci Code
da vinci code.author: Dan Brown
da vinci code.why: A symbologist chases secrets across Europe in a breathless conspiracy thriller; some readers found it mind-blowing.

westing game.title: The Westing Game
westing game.author: Ellen Raskin
westing game.why: Sixteen heirs to a rich man are paired to solve his murder; a children's puzzle mystery loved by adults.

sympathizer.title: The Sympathizer
sympathizer.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
sympathizer.why: A communist double agent after the Vietnam War, told in confession; a Pulitzer winner, darkly funny.

lord of the flies.title: Lord of the Flies
lord of the flies.author: William Golding
lord of the flies.why: Boys stranded on an island descend into savagery; short classic often read in school.

alchemised.title: Alchemised
alchemised.author: SenLinYu
alchemised.why: A dark necromancy and war romance that readers devoured and rated highly.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.author: Alan Moore
jerusalem.why: A vast, experimental novel of a working-class English town across time, with its own languages; rewarding but exhausting.

i claudius.title: I, Claudius
i claudius.author: Robert Graves
i claudius.why: The Roman emperor's story told with wit and intrigue; easy to read and fun.

brother.title: Brother
brother.author: Ania Ahlborn
brother.why: A southern horror about two brothers and a nightmare family, with twists and a final chapter that surprises.

three men in a boat.title: Three Men in a Boat (to say nothing of the dog)
three men in a boat.author: Jerome Klapka Jérôme
three men in a boat.why: Three friends and a dog row up the Thames in a comic Victorian classic; still funny.

art thief.title: The Art Thief
art thief.author: Michael Finkel
art thief.why: The true story of a prolific art thief, told like a thriller; short and engaging.

hiroshima.title: Hiroshima
hiroshima.author: John Hersey
hiroshima.why: Six survivors tell what happened when the atomic bomb fell on Hiroshima; a short reportage classic.

sociopath.title: Sociopath
sociopath.author: Patric Gagne
sociopath.why: A woman who is diagnosed as a sociopath explains her inner life and how she lives with it.

inkheart.title: Inkheart
inkheart.author: Cornelia Funke
inkheart.why: A girl who reads characters out of books; the first of a trilogy for fantasy-loving children.

raw shark texts.title: The Raw Shark Texts
raw shark texts.author: Steven Hall
raw shark texts.why: A man loses his memory to a creature that eats thoughts; a puzzle-like thriller like Memento.

world according to garp.title: The world according to Garp
world according to garp.author: John Irving
world according to garp.why: The life of a writer and his mother, a feminist icon, full of black comedy and tragedy.

mists of avalon.title: The Mists of Avalon
mists of avalon.author: Marion Zimmer Bradley
mists of avalon.why: The Arthurian legend told from the women's view; a favourite, though readers note problems with its author.

red tent.title: The Red Tent
red tent.author: Anita Diamant
red tent.why: The story of Dinah, a girl from the Bible, told by her; a women's life in the ancient world.

stories of your life and others.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
stories of your life and others.author: Ted Chiang
stories of your life and others.why: Chiang's thoughtful short stories including the basis for Arrival; clever and moving.

semiosis.title: Semiosis
semiosis.author: Sue Burke
semiosis.why: Generations of colonists on a distant planet, interacting with intelligent bamboo; praised as a late discovery.

heaven.title: Heaven
heaven.author: Mieko Kawakami
heaven.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

neverwhere.title: Neverwhere
neverwhere.author: Neil Gaiman
neverwhere.why: A man discovers a hidden London beneath the city; readers loved it from age 14 on.

people in the trees.title: The People in the Trees
people in the trees.author: Hanya Yanagihara
people in the trees.why: A doctor's memoir of a tropical island and what his research caused; unsettling, incredible prose.

filth.title: Filth
filth.author: Irvine Welsh
filth.why: A corrupt Edinburgh policeman narrated partly by his tapeworm; filthy, grim and unusual.

woman in white.title: The Woman in White
woman in white.author: Wilkie Collins
woman in white.why: A mysterious woman in white, a sinister count and a puzzle; an early Victorian sensation novel.

eye of the world.title: The Eye of the World
eye of the world.author: Robert Jordan
eye of the world.why: The first volume of a vast fantasy epic; a favourite among teenage readers who loved the world.

white teeth.title: White Teeth
white teeth.author: Zadie Smith
white teeth.why: Two families in London over generations; funny, warm and well noted.

on writing.title: On Writing
on writing.author: Stephen King
on writing.why: King's memoir and writing advice; readers value it as both a life story and a practical guide.

lesser dead.title: The Lesser Dead
lesser dead.author: Christopher Buehlman
lesser dead.why: A hard-to-describe vampire story set in New York in the 1970s; fans insist you go in blind.

sarum.title: Sarum
sarum.author: Edward Rutherford
sarum.why: The history of Salisbury and its area from the Ice Age to modern times, told through families.

momo.title: Momo
momo.author: Michael Ende
momo.why: A girl in an amphitheatre fights time thieves who steal people's hours; a short fable about valuing time.

shipping news.title: The Shipping News
shipping news.author: Annie Proulx
shipping news.why: A failing man takes his family to a harsh Newfoundland and finds a new life; rich, quirky prose.

inferno.title: Inferno
inferno.author: Larry Niven and Jerry Pournelle
inferno.why: A modern writer is guided through a Dante-style hell; a fan favourite among Niven works.

100 years of solitude.title: 100 Years of Solitude
100 years of solitude.author: Gabriel García Márquez
100 years of solitude.why: The Buendía family across a century in a town called Macondo; magical realism's best known book.

starfish.title: Starfish
starfish.author: Peter Watts
starfish.why: Engineers live at the bottom of the sea, and the dark gets to them; dark, atmospheric hard SF.

chronicles of narnia.title: The Chronicles of Narnia
chronicles of narnia.author: C. S. Lewis
chronicles of narnia.why: Children enter a world of talking animals and a lion; a lifelong favourite for many readers.

winters tale.title: Winter's Tale
winters tale.author: Mark Helprin
winters tale.why: A magical New York across centuries; ornate and moving, though the film failed the book.

turn of the screw.title: The Turn of the Screw
turn of the screw.author: Henry James
turn of the screw.why: A governess and the ghostly children in her care; ambiguous and short, the great ghost story.

boy parts.title: Boy Parts
boy parts.author: Eliza Clark
boy parts.why: A photographer lures men into her flat in a dark, unreliable satire; recommended.

life of pi.title: Life of Pi
life of pi.author: Yann Martel
life of pi.why: A boy shares a lifeboat with a tiger; a story that makes readers consider belief.

musashi.title: Musashi
musashi.author: Eiji Yoshikawa
musashi.why: A real samurai's life from violent youth to wise master; recommended to Shogun fans.

septology.title: Septology
septology.author: Jon Fosse
septology.why: One long sentence through a painter's life, faith and death; hard and unforgettable.

shadow of the torturer.title: The Shadow of the Torturer
shadow of the torturer.author: Gene Wolfe
shadow of the torturer.why: A torturer's apprentice in a dying far-future world, written in an elaborate style; first volume of a classic series.

memory.title: Memory
memory.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
memory.why: A mercenary-hero's story in a long, beloved space series; readers re-read Bujold often.

fall.title: Fall
fall.author: Albert Camus
fall.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

ella enchanted.title: Ella Enchanted
ella enchanted.author: Gail Carson Levine
ella enchanted.why: A girl is cursed to obey every command in this fairy-tale retelling; a favourite from childhood.

shroud.title: Shroud
shroud.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
shroud.why: Humans and a mysterious alien world meet in this recent Tchaikovsky novel; the author is a modern favourite.

jesus son.title: Jesus' Son.
jesus son.author: Denis Johnson
jesus son.why: Linked stories of drug-ridden misfits with rare grace; strange but moving.

sunshine.title: Sunshine
sunshine.author: Robin McKinley
sunshine.why: A baker in a world of vampires gets involved in a mess; makes you hungry for baked goods.

paradise lost.title: Paradise Lost
paradise lost.author: John Milton
paradise lost.why: Milton's epic poem of Satan's fall and the Fall of man; amazing and tough.
